title: From cylinder to device-ready surface
caption: Mechanical steps create the shape; chemical steps remove damage and contamination before final qualification. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Crop and size
nodes.detail: Prepare a controlled cylindrical crystal body.

nodes.label: Slice and flatten
nodes.detail: Create discs and correct their geometry.

nodes.label: Etch, polish and clean
nodes.detail: Remove damaged material and finish the surface.

nodes.label: Inspect and pack
nodes.detail: Qualify geometry, defects and cleanliness.

source.heading: The Process Flow at a Glance

title: Thickness is a mechanical design variable
caption: A larger or thinner wafer bends more easily under load; handling strength and usable material must be balanced. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Diameter
nodes.detail: A larger unsupported span increases bending sensitivity.

nodes.label: Thickness
nodes.detail: A thicker plate resists bending more strongly.

nodes.label: Support geometry
nodes.detail: Pins, rings and chucks change how the load is carried.

source.heading: Why 775 µm: Wafer Thickness and Mechanics

title: Separate growth transitions from usable crystal
caption: Cropping removes crown and tail while ingot quality checks locate acceptable material along the body. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: As-grown ingot
nodes.detail: Neck, shoulder, body and tail have different geometries.

nodes.label: Inspect the body
nodes.detail: Electrical and defect measurements locate usable regions.

nodes.label: Crop and section
nodes.detail: Cut away transition and rejected regions.

nodes.label: Qualified blocks
nodes.detail: Accepted cylinders proceed to diameter finishing.

title: Grind beneath the deepest surface ripple
caption: Rotating the ingot against an abrasive wheel creates a consistent diameter, rather than merely smoothing the highest ridges. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: As-grown surface
nodes.detail: Growth leaves diameter variation and ripples.

nodes.label: Grinding wheel
nodes.detail: Abrasive contact removes the outer material.

nodes.label: Sized cylinder
nodes.detail: The finished diameter fits wafering and handling specifications.

title: Transfer crystal orientation into a visible reference
caption: Diffraction identifies the lattice orientation; the notch lets subsequent tools orient the wafer consistently. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Determine lattice direction
nodes.detail: X-ray measurements locate crystal orientation.

nodes.label: Machine the notch
nodes.detail: A physical reference is cut into the crystal.

nodes.label: Align in the fab
nodes.detail: Tools use the notch to orient the wafer.

title: One moving wire becomes a parallel cutting web
caption: A wire wound over grooved guides creates many adjacent cuts; material between finished slices becomes kerf. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Wire web
nodes.detail: Repeated spans form closely spaced cutting paths.

nodes.label: Ingot feed
nodes.detail: The block advances into the moving wire.

nodes.label: Separated slices
nodes.detail: Discs emerge between neighboring cuts.

nodes.label: Kerf loss
nodes.detail: Silicon removed by the cuts cannot remain in the slices.

title: Lapping: work both wafer faces together
caption: In double-side lapping, abrasive slurry works between two plates while a carrier moves the wafer. Double-disk grinding uses opposed abrasive wheels and different support, as described in the text. Schematic section; thicknesses and clearances exaggerated.

nodes.label: Upper tool surface
nodes.detail: The upper plate or wheel removes material.

nodes.label: Wafer in carrier
nodes.detail: Controlled motion distributes abrasion over the faces.

nodes.label: Lower tool surface
nodes.detail: The opposing tool constrains and processes the other side.

title: A rounded edge removes a crack-prone corner
caption: The edge profile reduces stress concentration and particle shedding during later thermal processing and handling. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Sharp as-cut corner
nodes.detail: A fragile edge can chip and start a crack.

nodes.label: Profiled edge
nodes.detail: Controlled rounding removes the vulnerable geometry.

nodes.label: Later thermal cycle
nodes.detail: The finished edge must survive stress during processing.

title: Chemical removal must reach below the damage
caption: Before the damage-removal etch, cracks occupy a surface region rather than a separate material film. Chemistry removes that entire affected region without introducing new abrasive damage. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Damaged surface region
nodes.detail: The etch removes the region containing abrasive damage.

nodes.label: Sound underlying silicon
nodes.detail: Undisturbed crystal remains after sufficient material is removed.

title: A mark connects the wafer to its process history
caption: Wafer identity links later problems to earlier crystal and finishing conditions. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Write the identity
nodes.detail: A controlled laser mark labels the wafer.

nodes.label: Read the mark
nodes.detail: Tools associate the physical disc with its record.

nodes.label: Trace the history
nodes.detail: Records connect the wafer to ingot and process equipment.

title: CMP alternates surface chemistry and mechanical removal
caption: The pad does not simply grind bare silicon: chemistry modifies the surface and particles shear the softened material away. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Reactive liquid
nodes.detail: The slurry hydrates and modifies the surface.

nodes.label: Softened surface layer
nodes.detail: A thin chemically altered region forms.

nodes.label: Pad and particles
nodes.detail: Contact removes the reacted material.

nodes.label: Fresh surface
nodes.detail: Newly exposed silicon repeats the polishing cycle.

returnLabel: Freshly exposed silicon reacts again while polishing continues

title: Finish roughness after establishing flatness
caption: Touch polishing removes the remaining haze and fine scratches with gentler conditions; edge cleanliness still matters. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Double-side polished wafer
nodes.detail: The overall flat geometry is already established.

nodes.label: Soft pad and fine slurry
nodes.detail: A gentler final pass reduces fine surface texture.

nodes.label: Mirror surface
nodes.detail: Lower scattering reveals the smoother finish.

nodes.label: Clean edge and surface
nodes.detail: Remove residues before qualification.

source.heading: Polishing II: Final Front-Side Mirror Polish and the Edge

title: Thickness removal is a planned budget
caption: The section's worked example assigns material removal across grinding, damage etch and final polish; this drawing intentionally does not scale those amounts. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Raw slice
nodes.detail: The starting disc includes finishing allowance.

nodes.label: Grinding stock
nodes.detail: Mechanical removal establishes flatter geometry.

nodes.label: Damage-removal etch
nodes.detail: Chemistry consumes the disturbed surface.

nodes.label: Final polish allowance
nodes.detail: Finishing reaches the target thickness and surface quality.

title: Different cleaning steps remove different contaminants
caption: The cleaning sequence combines particle, organic and metallic contamination control before controlled rinsing and drying. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Organic and particle clean
nodes.detail: Surface chemistry loosens common polishing residues.

nodes.label: Oxide and metal control
nodes.detail: Selected chemistries remove unwanted surface species.

nodes.label: Ultrapure rinse
nodes.detail: Clean water removes remaining process chemicals.

nodes.label: Controlled drying
nodes.detail: Dry without leaving spots or new contamination.

source.heading: Cleaning: The RCA Sequence and Drying

title: Flatness has several meanings
caption: Whole-wafer shape and local thickness variation can affect lithography differently; the reference plane matters when interpreting a specification. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Thickness variation
nodes.detail: Compare the thickest and thinnest local regions.

nodes.label: Bow and warp
nodes.detail: The free wafer departs from a reference shape.

nodes.label: Local site flatness
nodes.detail: Exposure fields must remain within a usable focus range.

title: Turn scattered light into a defect map
caption: A scanning laser and collection optics locate surface scatterers; the signal is interpreted rather than being a direct photograph of every defect. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Illumination spot
nodes.detail: The moving beam samples the wafer surface.

nodes.label: Surface scatterer
nodes.detail: Particles or defects redirect part of the light.

nodes.label: Collection and detection
nodes.detail: Sensors record the scattered signal.

nodes.label: Wafer defect map
nodes.detail: Positions and signal classes support qualification.

title: Three ways to add substrate value
caption: Epitaxy, annealing and SOI processing modify different aspects of the starting wafer rather than representing interchangeable grades. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Epitaxial wafer
nodes.detail: A controlled crystalline surface layer is grown.

nodes.label: Annealed wafer
nodes.detail: Thermal treatment alters near-surface defect behavior.

nodes.label: SOI wafer
nodes.detail: A buried insulating layer separates device silicon from the handle.

source.heading: Beyond Polished: Epitaxial, Annealed, and SOI Wafers

title: A monitor wafer can return to service
caption: Monitor and dummy wafers support process control without becoming shipped circuits; reclamation restores only suitable wafers. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Monitor the process
nodes.detail: Use a wafer to assess tool contamination or film behavior.

nodes.label: Read the result
nodes.detail: Measurements qualify the process or reveal drift.

nodes.label: Strip and reclaim
nodes.detail: Remove films and restore usable surface conditions.

nodes.label: Reuse when qualified
nodes.detail: Return the wafer to an appropriate non-product role.

returnLabel: Only wafers that pass reclaim qualification return to service

title: Protect the surface across the shipping boundary
caption: A shipping container and a fab carrier solve different transport problems; cleanliness must survive the handoff. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Qualified wafers
nodes.detail: Accepted surfaces are ready for protected handling.

nodes.label: Shipping container
nodes.detail: A FOSB protects wafers during transportation.

nodes.label: Incoming handling
nodes.detail: The fab receives and checks the shipment.

nodes.label: Fab carrier
nodes.detail: A FOUP supports controlled movement and tool docking.

title: A wafer specification joins several measurements
caption: No single surface measurement certifies a prime wafer: geometry, electrical properties and defect limits must all satisfy the intended process. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Geometry
nodes.detail: Diameter, thickness and flatness constrain tool compatibility.

nodes.label: Electrical properties
nodes.detail: Doping and resistivity suit the device design.

nodes.label: Surface quality
nodes.detail: Particles and defects must meet acceptance limits.

nodes.label: Customer specification
nodes.detail: Together the requirements define a qualified product.

source.heading: A Representative 300 mm Prime Wafer Specification

title: Wafer demand follows fab loading and inventory
caption: The wafer supplier's shipments depend on customer usage and inventory decisions; capacity and qualification make adjustments slow. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Fab production
nodes.detail: Process starts consume fresh wafers.

nodes.label: Customer inventory
nodes.detail: Stocks buffer differences between orders and usage.

nodes.label: Supplier shipments
nodes.detail: Orders draw on qualified wafer capacity.

nodes.label: Capacity decisions
nodes.detail: Investment responds to expectations with a delay.

returnLabel: Capacity and inventory decisions affect later production
